chapter: Hurry On Down, Capitol and New York
title: Nat King Cole as a person and Natalie Cole's style
summary: She praises Nat as a beloved man and artist and comments that Natalie Cole once sounded like Aretha Franklin.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: was one of the better loved people in the business, you know. I would compare Nat's -- people loving him and really appreciating him to Crosby or Sinatra or any people of that calibre, you know. I held him in very high esteem as an artist, and as a person. He was a wonderful man. He was just a very beautiful person, and you know, he would not -- now, he would not have condoned anything like that. He wouldn't have said anything to really harm or hurt anyone, Nat wouldn't. He was a great artist, a great artist and a great person, and I'm very happy for his daughter today, who has made a big name for herself, you know, in a different capacity, completely different. Her type of singing isn't the type of singing that I would run around or break my neck to hear, but nevertheless, she is in the business, and she's doing, as the kids say today, she's doing her thing her way, and she has proven herself to be a real trooper and a wonderful girl, a marvelous girl.
She's got a talent, and I think whatever she does it's done tastefully.

It's her, you know. She's not trying to do anybody else. Well, there's one time -- I have to take that back. There was one time I thought very much she sounded -- she was greatly influenced by Aretha Franklin. That was my personal opinion. I very much -- you know, I listened and

said, 'My God.' I couldn't hardly tell, really, that it wasn't Aretha, because Aretha had been so big for so long, you know, and this was all you could hear, and when Natalie Cole -- to me she reminded me very much of Aretha Franklin. I'm not saying that she -- that she was copying her. I'm not saying that, but I'm just saying the style was similar, to me. But I think she has gotten away from that, you know, now.
